payload.note: REVERSE_PHYSICS_WHAT_REPLACES_A_COUNT closed by REVERSE_PHYSICS_RELATIONAL_COUNT_ROCQ_V1. A RELATIVE count nu(U,V) survives the dilation argument - it acts on both arguments, so nu(ball r, ball s) depends only on r/s, which is exactly what conformal invariance always says. With the chain rule, f(t)=nu(ball t, ball 1) is MULTIPLICATIVE, hence f(2^n)=f(2)^n: the whole family is generated by ONE NUMBER. So what survives of 'how many DOFs' is not a function on regions but a single scaling exponent. And the two results are one phenomenon: assuming an absolute reference region forces f(2)=1 and the exponent collapses, so the exponent is nonzero PRECISELY because no conformally invariant reference exists. Their '#states = prod #confDOF' should become ADDITIVITY OF THE EXPONENT - stated, not proved. A negative control confirms non-degeneracy without the reference assumption. Boundary: exponent not shown positive or equal to a dimension (monotonicity not assumed), dyadic scales only, additivity reading unproved. Gate 17 green 0 red, 93/93 closed, 12 negative controls. New gate: REVERSE_PHYSICS_EXPONENT_ADDITIVITY.
